page: Amazon Web Services c6id.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 2.0 GB per vCPU, and is provisioned with 3800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. It provides a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps without GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance, highlighted by top-quartile results in PassMark CPU tests, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. The processor includes hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and VAES, driving strong performance in encryption routines and database operations. Text generation benchmarks for small and medium language models also rank in the top quartile, while single-core execution and raw memory bandwidth tests place in the middle 50% tier.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio paired with 3.8 TB of fast local NVMe storage, the c6id.16xlarge delivers substantial compute density alongside high-capacity local disk IOPS. The trade-off is an instance-store architecture that requires managing ephemeral storage lifecycles. This profile suits compute-intensive workloads that require low-latency scratch space or fast local caching, including high-concurrency software build pipelines, distributed database engines, batch media processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It offers 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, alongside 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The system achieves top-quartile performance in multi-threaded compilation, ray tracing, database operations, and encryption tests, backed by AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides high compute density, while the bundled NVMe array provides large, high-speed ephemeral local capacity. The c6id.16xlarge is well tailored for intensive tasks requiring fast local disk access and dedicated multi-core compute, such as continuous integration build fleets, distributed database nodes, and static web serving.
